page.title: OpenCloud Backup Destinations
page.subtitle: Back up containers to an OpenCloud instance via WebDAV (RFC 4918). OpenCloud is a Nextcloud-compatible server (same protocol surface) so the plugin uses the Nextcloud WebDAV paths (/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/). Two auth modes: OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow or direct app-password authentication. Chunked uploads use Content-Range PUT, supported server-side by OpenCloud's WebDAV.
page.registerHint: Click Test connection to verify the WebDAV endpoint is reachable and the credentials are valid.

fields.refreshToken: Refresh token (delivered by the OAuth consent flow)
fields.folderId: Folder under the user root (blank for the user root)

error.noSecret: OAuth client secret or app password is required.

form.introBody: Generate an app password in Personal settings → Security → App passwords, or register an OAuth 2.0 client under admin settings. Either approach works over HTTP Basic auth on every WebDAV call. McHarbor stores the secret encrypted at rest.
form.hostHelp: Base URL of the OpenCloud instance, e.g. https://cloud.example.com. Do not add a trailing slash.
form.clientIdHelp: OAuth 2.0 client_id from OpenCloud admin → Settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients. Leave blank if you use an app password.
form.clientSecretHelp: Either the OAuth 2.0 client_secret, or an app password from OpenCloud Personal settings → Security → App passwords. Both work over HTTP Basic auth on every WebDAV call.
form.basePathHelp: Optional subfolder under the user's OpenCloud Files root.
form.apiPathHelp: Override the WebDAV path. Defaults to /remote.php/dav/files/{username}/. Set this only if your OpenCloud sits behind a reverse proxy that rewrites the WebDAV path.

setup.title: OpenCloud setup guide
setup.step1: In OpenCloud, open Personal settings → Security → App passwords. (Admins can enable this for the whole instance via Settings → Security.) Give the app password a descriptive name (e.g. mcharbor-backups) and click Create app password.
setup.step2: Copy the username (the account you want backups to land under) and the app password OpenCloud just generated. Both are case-sensitive.
setup.step3: In McHarbor, paste the OpenCloud base URL (e.g. https://cloud.example.com — no trailing slash), the username, and the app password into the form on the left. Optional: set a folder under the user root (e.g. Backups/2026) and let McHarbor create intermediate folders automatically.
setup.step4: Click Test connection to round-trip a probe file in the resolved folder. The plugin performs an HTTP Basic-authenticated WebDAV PROPFIND against /remote.php/dav/files/{username}/ to confirm the destination is reachable and the credentials are valid.
setup.step5: Optional: switch to a delegated OAuth flow by creating an OAuth 2.0 client in OpenCloud admin → Settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients. Set the redirect URI to your McHarbor host's /api/storage-locations/oauth/callback. Generate a client secret, paste both into the form, then click Connect to grant consent. The plugin stores the refresh token and refreshes it transparently on every backup run.
setup.step6: Trigger a backup. The plugin uploads the archive via WebDAV using Content-Range chunked PUT so even 10+ GB backups stream without buffering the entire payload in memory at once. OpenCloud's WebDAV server reassembles the chunks server-side.
